idiom_name: rayon par_iter/scope (std::thread::scope + channels as the manual form)
implementation_notes: Rayon is the default realization: par_iter turns a collection into parallel tasks over a work-stealing pool, scope spawns tasks that may borrow the environment and joins them before the scope ends, and ThreadPoolBuilder sizes or names the pool - aggregation is an ordinary iterator reduction over the returned values, so there is no shared mutable state to protect. The std-only form is std::thread::scope plus a channel (or chunked spawns) when a dependency cannot be added, and tokio's JoinSet plays the same role for async code; rayon's data-race-free guarantee comes from the closure returning its partial result rather than writing to shared memory.
pitfalls: A rayon task must not block waiting for another task's result: use join for already-spawned work, because blocking a pool thread can deadlock when the dependency is still queued.
A panic in a worker surfaces when the result is collected (join unwinds or rayon aborts the pool); shared mutable state via Arc<Mutex<_>> reintroduces the contention the pattern removes.
par_bridge over a serial iterator adds synchronisation cost, and nested rayon calls can oversubscribe the pool if a scoped thread pool is not used.
